readmeExcerpt:
# Claude HUD A Claude Code plugin that shows what's happening: context usage, rate limits, active tools, running agents, and todo progress, always visible below your input. > 🌐 English | [中文文档](README.zh.md) ## Install Inside Claude Code, run: ``` /plugin marketplace add jarrodwatts/claude-hud /plugin install claude-hud /reload-plugins /hud ``` `/hud` checks your setup and points your status line at the HUD, after asking you. It needs Node.js 22.18 or later; if yours is older, `/hud` finds a newer one on your machine or helps you install one.
Prefer the terminal? ```bash claude plugin marketplace add jarrodwatts/claude-hud claude plugin install claude-hud@claude-hud ``` Then run `/reload-plugins` and `/hud` inside a session.
**Updates:** Claude Code doesn't auto-update third-party plugins by default. To turn it on, run `/plugin`, open **Marketplaces**, select **claude-hud**, and choose **Enable auto-update**. Or update by hand with `claude plugin marketplace update claude-hud` and `claude plugin update claude-hud@claude-hud`, then `/reload-plugins`. You don't need to set it up again. ## What You See The default is two lines: ``` [Opus] │ my-project git:(main*) Context █████░░░░░ 45% │ Usage ██░░░░░░░░ 25% (resets in 1h 30m) ``` - **Line 1**: model, a provider label when one is detected (`Bedrock`, `Vertex`, `MiniMax`), project path, and git branch. - **Line 2**: context used (green, then yellow, then red as it fills) and your subscriber rate limits. Optional lines include tools, agents and todos, plus about a hundred other options: ``` ◐ Edit: auth.ts | ✓ Read ×3 | ✓ Grep ×2 ← tools ◐ explore [haiku]: Finding auth code (2m 15s) ← agents ▸ Fix authentication bug (2/5) ← todos ``` ## Change It, Fix It, Report It Ask Claude, or type `/hud` and say what you want: "show tool activity", "use the compact layout", "the HUD is blank", "the context bar looks wrong". Claude looks up the options, shows you a preview, and saves the change once you approve it. `/hud` also undoes the last change, replays the last real render to explain what you see, and, for a real bug, writes a scrubbed report that you read in full before anything is filed. Settings live in `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json` (under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` if set). To turn the HUD off for one session, start Claude Code with `CLAUDE_HUD_DISABLE=1`. ## Security The HUD's logic runs in a locked-down Node process. Node's permission model blocks it from starting programs, reading your credentials, and writing anywhere but its own data folder. An import fence keeps Node's network modules and globals out of its reach; that fence blocks every way out found so far, and is tested against each one on every change. A small separate file runs the fixed `git`, `jj` and memory commands it needs. The HUD reads Claude Code's stdin, the session transcript, Claude config files, and git or jj metadata for the current directory, and calls no undocumented APIs. `--extra-cmd` runs a shell command on every refresh and puts its output on the first line. It is ignored unless `CLAUDE_HUD_ALLOW_EXTRA_CMD=1` is set in the HUD's environment. Treat it as arbitrary code execution and never use a command from an untrusted source. ## Requirements - Claude Code v2.1.260 or later - Node.js 22.18 or later (Bun can start the HUD, which then runs on Node) ## Development ```bash git clone https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud cd claude-hud npm ci && npm test ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). ## Star History

releases.name: v0.15.0
releases.body:
### Security
- A repository's own git config can no longer run a command when you open Claude Code in it. In 0.14.2 and earlier, a booby-trapped repo could do this through a partial clone's automatic fetch, or through a filter driver whose name git couldn't be told to skip. Git now never reaches the network for the HUD, and the HUD skips git for a repo whose filters it can't switch off. Thanks to @yx64 (GHSA-f7gq-pcm8-rxr4) and @mrthankyou (GHSA-25hg-g83m-4w35) for reporting these privately.

### Changed
- `/hud` replaces `/claude-hud:setup` and `/claude-hud:configure`. Ask Claude to set the HUD up, show or change a setting (with a preview first), check what's wrong, or prepare a bug report with private details removed.
- The HUD now runs straight from its TypeScript source and needs Node.js 22.18 or newer. On older Node, the status line shows one line asking you to type `/hud`, which helps you upgrade. Bun can still launch it.
- The HUD's code runs in a locked-down Node process that can't start other programs or write outside its own folder. One small, separately reviewed file runs git and the other programs the HUD needs.
- A config value the HUD can't use now shows one line end

releases.name: v0.14.2
releases.body:
### Fixed
- The HUD now finds the plugin when `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` moves Claude Code's plugin folder. Before, the status line was empty or ran an old install left in the default location. If you set this variable, run `/claude-hud:setup` again once to refresh the launcher it copied (#838).

releases.name: v0.14.1
releases.body:
### Fixed
- On Windows, Ctrl+click on the project name or a changed file now opens paths with non-ASCII characters, such as `D:\桌面\project`. Windows decoded the percent-encoded link with the system code page and opened nothing (#839, #840).

releases.name: v0.14.0
releases.body:
### Added
- `display.showLaunchDir` option. Once Claude moves deeper than `pathLevels` shows, the project path starts with the directory Claude Code was launched in, e.g. `my-repo › src`. Off by default (#835, #836).

releases.name: v0.13.1
releases.body:
### Fixed
- Session names, the Claude Code version, output style, effort, model and advisor names, the advisor override, scoped usage labels, failing MCP server names, the auth user, and jj labels no longer cut an emoji or flag in half when they hit their length cap (#830).

readmeHtml:
Claude HUD

A Claude Code plugin that shows what's happening: context usage, rate limits, active tools, running agents, and todo progress, always visible below your input.

🌐 English | 中文文档

Install

Inside Claude Code, run:

/plugin marketplace add jarrodwatts/claude-hud
/plugin install claude-hud
/reload-plugins
/hud

/hud checks your setup and points your status line at the HUD, after asking you. It needs Node.js 22.18 or later; if yours is older, /hud finds a newer one on your machine or helps you install one.

Prefer the terminal? 
claude plugin marketplace add jarrodwatts/claude-hud
claude plugin install claude-hud@claude-hud

Then run /reload-plugins and /hud inside a session.

Updates: Claude Code doesn't auto-update third-party plugins by default. To turn it on, run /plugin, open Marketplaces, select claude-hud, and choose Enable auto-update. Or update by hand with claude plugin marketplace update claude-hud and claude plugin update claude-hud@claude-hud, then /reload-plugins. You don't need to set it up again.

What You See

The default is two lines:

[Opus] │ my-project git:(main*)
Context █████░░░░░ 45% │ Usage ██░░░░░░░░ 25% (resets in 1h 30m)
  • Line 1: model, a provider label when one is detected (Bedrock, Vertex, MiniMax), project path, and git branch.
  • Line 2: context used (green, then yellow, then red as it fills) and your subscriber rate limits.

Optional lines include tools, agents and todos, plus about a hundred other options:

◐ Edit: auth.ts | ✓ Read ×3 | ✓ Grep ×2        ← tools
◐ explore [haiku]: Finding auth code (2m 15s)    ← agents
▸ Fix authentication bug (2/5)                   ← todos

Change It, Fix It, Report It

Ask Claude, or type /hud and say what you want: "show tool activity", "use the compact layout", "the HUD is blank", "the context bar looks wrong". Claude looks up the options, shows you a preview, and saves the change once you approve it. /hud also undoes the last change, replays the last real render to explain what you see, and, for a real bug, writes a scrubbed report that you read in full before anything is filed.

Settings live in ~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/config.json (under $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR if set). To turn the HUD off for one session, start Claude Code with CLAUDE_HUD_DISABLE=1.

Security

The HUD's logic runs in a locked-down Node process. Node's permission model blocks it from starting programs, reading your credentials, and writing anywhere but its own data folder. An import fence keeps Node's network modules and globals out of its reach; that fence blocks every way out found so far, and is tested against each one on every change. A small separate file runs the fixed git, jj and memory commands it needs. The HUD reads Claude Code's stdin, the session transcript, Claude config files, and git or jj metadata for the current directory, and calls no undocumented APIs.

--extra-cmd runs a shell command on every refresh and puts its output on the first line. It is ignored unless CLAUDE_HUD_ALLOW_EXTRA_CMD=1 is set in the HUD's environment. Treat it as arbitrary code execution and never use a command from an untrusted source.

Requirements

  • Claude Code v2.1.260 or later
  • Node.js 22.18 or later (Bun can start the HUD, which then runs on Node)

Development

git clone https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud
cd claude-hud
npm ci && npm test

See CONTRIBUTING.md.

License

MIT. See LICENSE.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A terminal HUD designed for Claude Code to monitor context and tokens in AI coding agents.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Claude HUD is a developer tool that provides a persistent terminal heads-up display specifically designed to accompany the official Claude Code CLI tool. It tackles the core issue of "context blindness" that developers face when working with AI coding agents. While the agent runs, the HUD provides a real-time, visual breakdown of the token consumption, active file context, memory utilization, and cost metrics. It intercepts the background communication and logging of the Claude Code tool to extract these metrics without interfering with its operation. This allows developers to actively manage their context window and API spending during long, complex autonomous coding sessions.
keyFeatures: Real-time token monitoring: Continuously tracks input and output token consumption precisely during active Claude Code sessions.
Context visualization: Displays exactly which files and directories the agent is currently holding actively in its context window.
Cost tracking: Calculates and displays running API costs based on token usage metrics and current model pricing.
Non-blocking architecture: Runs safely in parallel with the main Claude Code process without interrupting its execution flow.
Memory insights: Visualizes the agent's internal memory state and tracked variables during complex coding tasks.

useCases.title: Context management
useCases.description: Monitor the exact files in the agent's context window to prevent the model from becoming overwhelmed and hallucinating.

useCases.title: Cost optimization
useCases.description: Track the real-time financial cost of an autonomous coding session to avoid unexpected API bills.

useCases.title: Agent debugging
useCases.description: Understand exactly what information the agent is looking at when it makes a mistake or gets stuck.

useCases.title: Workflow efficiency
useCases.description: Keep the HUD open in a side terminal to maintain a clear overview of the agent's background activities.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers and developers who heavily utilize the official Claude Code CLI tool for autonomous development. It requires familiarity with terminal environments and AI coding workflows.
